newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago comfortable with EPS views.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago comfortable with EPS views.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp Chief Financial Officer Robert Rosholt told analysts that the company is comfortable with estimates that it will earn within a range of $1.12 to $1.17 per share in the first quarter of 1997 and in a range of $4.80 to $5 per share in fiscal 1997.
Rosholt also said the company's goals are to have earnings per share grow 11 to 13 percent per year and to generate return on equity greater than 18 percent.

A company spokesman said that the company expects to generate a return on equity (ROE) in the credit card business in 1997 that will be less than the 32 percent ROE in that business in 1996. He also said that the card business'
contribution to corporate earnings will be less than the 24 percent in 1997.
But, on the question of whether the after-tax net income from cards will be less this year than 1996's $347 million after-tax net income, the spokesman said "we're not saying."
Earlier, Executive Vice President Jerry Jurgensen said in response to a question that the card earings would be lower but he did not give an amount.
Jurgensen said the card busiess still remains very profitable.
